title: Faico: Faithful and Complete Knowledge Graph Augmented Reasoning

problem.claim: Knowledge-graph-augmented large language models are used for complex reasoning tasks.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often suffer from incomplete subgraph retrieval and inaccurate semantic alignment, hindering reasoning performance and answer quality.

contributions.claim: Faico is a knowledge-graph-enhanced reasoning framework targeting semantic faithfulness and structural completeness.
Faico separates model inference from graph traversal using a fine-tuned LLM-based relation type generator and a knowledge graph retriever.
Faico models reasoning subgraphs as k-bounded edge type subgraphs and uses a budget-dominance-based algorithm to identify the maximal such subgraph.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The framework is reported to provide comprehensive coverage of relevant multi-hop relations while reducing computational overhead.
On multiple KGQA benchmarks, the authors report improvements in effectiveness and efficiency over LLM-native and state-of-the-art knowledge-graph-augmented reasoning baselines.
The authors report more accurate and complete answers together with lower inference latency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge-graph augmentation is promising for complex reasoning with large language models.
Existing methods face incomplete retrieval and inaccurate semantic alignment.
Faico is introduced to address semantic faithfulness and structural completeness.
The framework combines relation type generation, knowledge graph retrieval, k-bounded edge type subgraphs, and maximal-subgraph search.
Experiments on multiple KGQA benchmarks report improved effectiveness and efficiency, more accurate and complete answers, and lower inference latency.

source_observation.claim: Separating semantic relation mapping from graph traversal is presented as a way to address inaccurate alignment and incomplete retrieval.

interpretation.claim: Reasoning pipelines may benefit from distinct components for semantic interpretation and structured search.

application.claim: Use a relation-type generation stage followed by constrained knowledge graph subgraph retrieval when multi-hop reasoning requires both semantic alignment and coverage.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition generalizes beyond the reported KGQA benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the KGQA benchmarks or report numerical results.
The abstract does not specify the relation type generator training data, model architecture, or retrieval budget.
The abstract does not provide ablation results or implementation details.
